summary: Created orchestrator/src/utils/persona_models.py with extract_persona_model_slugs(workspace_root) — stdlib-only YAML parsing via _extract_yaml_scalar() and _strip_inline_comment() helpers; loads default slug from _shared.yaml, builds number→stage_id map from workflow-manifest.json, globs [1-9]-*.yaml persona files, returns {stage_id: model_slug} for all 9 stages.

Created orchestrator/tests/test_persona_models.py with 27 tests across four classes: TestStripInlineComment (6), TestExtractYamlScalar (7), TestExtractPersonaModelSlugs (9 unit tests with tmp_path fixtures), TestRealWorkspace (4 integration tests against committed metadata). All 27 pass; 722-test full suite shows no regressions.

comments.note: persona_models.py intentionally skips manifest entries that have no corresponding YAML file (logs a warning). If future roles are added to the manifest before their YAML files are created, the returned dict will be silently incomplete. A caller-side assertion that len(result) == expected_count would make this failure loud at startup.

Edge-case stress tests run manually: empty _shared.yaml → ValueError (good); malformed manifest missing 'roles' → KeyError (obscure but acceptable); duplicate YAML number → last sorted file wins (deterministic); non-integer number field → warns and skips (correct); no persona files → returns empty dict without error.

comments.note: When workflow-manifest.json exists but has no 'roles' key, the function raises KeyError: 'roles'. A more descriptive error (e.g. ValueError with a human-readable message) would aid debugging. Not an AC violation.

If two YAML files share the same number (e.g. 1-aaa.yaml and 1-zzz.yaml both have 'number: 1'), the last file in sorted order silently wins. Behavior is deterministic but undocumented. Could add a duplicate-number warning log.

Empty persona metadata directory returns {} without error — consistent with the Developer's own implementation note about silent incompleteness. Caller-side assertion on len(result) == 9 recommended at startup as previously flagged.
